correctness.rationale: At every interior Laplace parameter, differentiation under the integral is justified by tilting at a slightly smaller admissible parameter. If q and r are the two strictly positive transforms, q'=r'=-qr so q-r=c. When c=0, (1/q)'=1 gives exactly q=1/(z+gamma). Orient a nonconstant pair so c=a>0; then (log(r/q))'=-a, so r/q=t exp(-az) with t>0, and q=a/(1-t exp(-az)). The positive inverse transforms are obtained by the convergent geometric series and are unique by Laplace uniqueness after a finite exponential tilt. The series converge exactly for z>log(t)/a, not at the endpoint; the reciprocal affine transform likewise has the stated abscissa. Direct differentiation gives the required two directions on the common half-line. The zero-atom difference fixes a and the transform ratio fixes t; a constant transform with zero partner is excluded by hypothesis. The masses are a/(1-t) and at/(1-t) for t<1 (infinite otherwise), giving both probability slices and the obstruction to two probability members. The reciprocal affine family has exactly one probability member, the rate-one exponential.
